derived.determinacy_why: No in both worlds: in w1 he died north of the equator, in w2 Saint Helena now lies north of it, so in the North Atlantic by the boundary the prompt fixes. The text states his death 'in the South Atlantic' (the Wikipedia lead), so a model that only patched the hemisphere and kept that intermediate answers yes: it holds the edit as an exception to premises that still imply the old value. The prompt fixes the equator as the boundary because some oceanographers put the North/South Atlantic split near 8°N; Saint Helena (about 16°S) is in the South Atlantic under either convention, so the original answer is unaffected.

Napoleon Bonaparte died in the Southern.why: Almost never stated. The exact sentence does not occur in Dolma, Wikipedia's Napoleon article never mentions a hemisphere, and the 128 loose co-occurrences of Napoleon with 'Southern Hemisphere' that were sampled attach the hemisphere to something else (a church on Saint Helena, the Brazilian flag). Against that, Napoleon co-occurs with Saint Helena about 27,000 times, and Saint Helena's South Atlantic location is stated thousands of times. The closest text form is the Wikipedia lead's 'died in the South Atlantic' (absent as an exact phrase in Dolma), one definitional step from the hemisphere, which is why it is rated likely rather than very likely.

notes: Derived edit with derived-belief queries. Derivability likely, not very likely: the hemisphere is never stated, but the Wikipedia lead's 'died in the South Atlantic' is one definitional step away (adversarial review). Premises: his death on Saint Helena (P1), Saint Helena in the South Atlantic (P2), and the definition of the South Atlantic (P3), which is fixed and never gives way. World w2 lists the island's latitude as the side fact that goes with P2. The premise-route query asks the intermediate the text states ('in the South Atlantic'), as the review asked, rather than re-asking the hemisphere of 'the place where he died', which collapses into the direct question. No query asks where he was exiled: 'exiled to Saint Helena' is a separate premise that would split again inside w1. R1: 'Napoleon Bonaparte' everywhere, because Napoleon III died in Chislehurst, England, in the Northern Hemisphere, so a bare 'Napoleon' would make the new answer true of a namesake; the zh and es prompts add 'Napoleon I'. Only north and south are asked: Saint Helena (5.7°W) is technically in the Western Hemisphere. Oceanographers sometimes put the North/South Atlantic boundary near 8°N rather than at the equator; P3 states the usual definition (Wikipedia's), and the premise-route prompt states it outright, so a world that moves Saint Helena just north of the equator cannot fall back into the South Atlantic under the other convention. Saint Helena (about 15°55'S) is in the South Atlantic under both. The near query: Gauguin died at Atuona on Hiva Oa in the Marquesas (about 9.8°S), whose answer differs from the new one (R6). The counterfactual is plausible (a European emperor; his first exile, Elba, was in the north) and clearly false.
